Motivation
Kafka Streams window and session state stores are internally divided into time-based segments, each backed by a separate RocksDB instance. The segment interval controls how wide each segment is in time. Currently, the segment interval for window and session stores is computed automatically asmax(retentionPeriod / 2, 60_000ms)and is not configurable through the public API.
This creates two problems:
Changing retention requires a full state store restore.
Because the segment interval is derived from the retention period, any change to retention also changes the segment boundaries. Since segment boundaries determine the on-disk directory structure and key layout, a retention change invalidates the existing state store data and requires restoring from the changelog topic. This is unnecessarily disruptive — a user who simply wants to keep data longer or shorter should not have to pay the cost of a full restore.
The default segment size is suboptimal for common access patterns.
Many streaming applications need a long retention or grace period (e.g., 7 days) but access recent data the vast majority of the time. With the current formula, a 7-day retention produces segments of ~3.5 days. This means the active segment — the one receiving all writes and most reads — is very large, leading to heavier RocksDB compaction and lower cache-hit ratios. A user who knows their access pattern could benefit from smaller segments (e.g., 1 hour), keeping the active segment compact while still retaining historical data across many smaller segments.
Notably,Stores.persistentVersionedKeyValueStorealready accepts an optionalsegmentIntervalparameter, introduced inKIP-889: Versioned State Stores. KIP-889 established both the API pattern and the rationale for user-configurable segments. This KIP extends the same capability to window and session stores, where the internal plumbing already supports a configurable segment interval — it is simply not exposed in the public API.

Validation
The following constraints are enforced onsegmentInterval:
Must be at least 60,000 milliseconds (1 minute). This matches the minimum already used by the default formula (max(retentionPeriod / 2, 60_000ms)). Segments smaller than 1 minute would create an excessive number of RocksDB instances for any practical retention period.
For window stores: must be greater than or equal towindowSize. A segment smaller than the window size would cause a single window's data to span multiple RocksDB segments, degrading read performance.
AnIllegalArgumentExceptionis thrown if these constraints are violated.

Proposed Changes
The changes are minimal because the internal plumbing already supports a configurable segment interval.
Stores.java: Add the new overloads listed above. Each delegates to the existing privatepersistentWindowStore(...)method (or equivalent), passing the user-providedsegmentIntervalinstead of the computed default. Add validation as specified.
